summary: We have developed an online platform to allow the average farmer to use the crop rotation system to make informed planting decisions. By inserting basic data such as Farm Name, Farm Size, Soil Type, Source of Irrigation and Previous Crop (GPS Location can also be inserted), next to you will have a dashboard showing crop recommendations, crop rotation visuals, 6 seasons of fertiliser cycles, irrigation comparisons, satellite imagery, audio based Plant Encyclopedia and a built in AI agricultural assistant called Jaafar. The platform allows an easy point of access to show them the satellite earth observations, local climate and agricultural science knowledge. The app does not simply recommend crops but shows how well the soil will be replenished after each crop and how much it will cost to grow. It will also tell farmers how much water is being used meaning they can see why certain crops are recommended. This solution is important because millions of smallholder farmers are guessing what to plant which causes rapid soil degradation, wasting irrigation water and unnecessary losses. We have made precision agriculture easily accessible to the average farmer, using an easy audio interface. This will help farmers keep their soil healthy, save crucial water and grow healthier and more profitable crops each season.
details:
What does our project do?

The web application allows farmers to make informed decisions when planting their crops via intelligent crop rotation. Farmers will provide some simple information about their land in the ‘My Land’ section such as: their land name, total area, soil type, irrigation type and what they last planted. Farmers may also choose to add their GPS location so that we can automatically provide them with their local environmental data and satellite imagery. The NextCrop algorithm then takes this information and produces a complete dashboard. This dashboard provides farmers with a summary of the details for the land they have added, a prioritized crop recommendation list showing the best to worst recommendation, a visual diagram showing the crop rotation cycle, a 6 season soil fertility forecast, a rough estimate of water requirements for each crop and local weather and satellite information.

What features does our project have?

This web application is a complete one stop shop for farmers. It provides them with an easy way to find out what crops to plant, the weather information and gives them accurate advice. The application is available in two languages (Arabic and English). There is also a plant encyclopedia which can be searched for different topics relating to planting, irrigation, fertilizing and diseases. This has the added feature of text to speech functionality to allow farmers (of any literacy level) to easily hear the advice. There is also a chatbot called ‘Jaafar,’ which can answer farmers questions. There is no need to purchase any expensive equipment to monitor the land.

What impact will our project have?

This web application was created so that everyday farmers and small scale farmers can easily understand and use the agricultural, weather and satellite data. We want to help farmers change from traditional farming to using data to make informed decisions. We want to raise awareness of crop rotation so that farmers can make informed decisions to keep their soils fertile in the long term.

What technologies/tools have we used?

Our application was created using AI to speed up our development. We used Gemini & Claude to help us with our coding, UI/UX and crop rotation logic. For our front end and decision making we used HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript. This provided a multi language application with interactive crop rotation diagrams and 6 season soil fertility forecasts. We also used GPS, satellite imagery, weather data, text to speech (multi language), and chatbot.

How creative and innovative is our project?

Instead of just recommending a crop to plant we have made it so that farmers can understand why they should plant that crop. We have created an easy to understand agronomy system which shows farmers how planting that crop will affect their soil fertility over 6 seasons. We have brought together satellite imagery, cost of growing crops and nutrients back into the soil to create a no equipment crop recommendation system. We have also included a text to speech plant encyclopedia and chatbot.

What have we considered?

When creating our recommendation system we considered how to balance sustainability with cost. We looked at 4 key factors. How much the previous crop had taken out of the soil, how much the soil would recover over multiple seasons, how much it would cost to grow each crop based on the total land area, how much water each crop would require based on the irrigation source. We also considered the GPS factors such as: GPS location, soil type, weather and satellite images.

Using satellite imagery and Agronomy we have created a simple to use voice enabled application. This means every farmer can understand how to keep their land safe, save water and grow healthier and more profitable crops.
